title: Restore SQLite startup after a native bundle is retired
goal: Replace a retired convenience bundle with initialization for the native engine the app already needs. Executed free Windows x64 system-provider route; encrypted/custom engines need separate compatibility proof. Current-release evidence is RC2, not GA.

selectionNotes: Applies when replacing bundle_winsqlite3 while retaining the Windows system native engine and unencrypted storage.
Windows x64 execution only. SQLitePCLRaw is external; encryption/paid alternatives are conditional decisions, never defaults. RC2 proof is not GA proof.

packages.reason: Use Core to avoid an automatically selected native bundle; observed pin 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105.

packages.name: SQLitePCLRaw.provider.winsqlite3
packages.reason: Explicit Windows system-library provider; core resolves to 3.0.5.

packageAssets: Current net11.0 selects Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core lib/net10.0/Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.dll, provider.winsqlite3 lib/netstandard2.0, and raw core lib/net8.0. No native runtime asset is packaged: Windows supplies winsqlite3.dll.
Previous net10.0 comparison selects Core10 lib/net8.0, bundle/provider.winsqlite3 2.1.11 and core2.1.13. The old bundle is a valid historical convenience, not a 3.x replacement.
providers: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core11 RC2 -> SQLitePCLRaw.core/provider.winsqlite3 3.0.5 -> Windows system winsqlite3.dll. SQLitePCLRaw is an external community dependency, not Microsoft-owned.
platforms: Windows x64 only, with Windows-supplied winsqlite3.dll; authoring execution loaded C:/Windows/System32/winsqlite3.dll, SQLite/file version 3.53.4. Native version and features vary with Windows servicing.
No UWP, classic Xamarin, MAUI, Linux, macOS, other architecture or encrypted-native execution is claimed. This is a modern desktop console route, not UWP guidance.
renderingModes: Not applicable: native console/database work; no renderer.
constraints: Use only where existing requirements already permit the Windows system engine, ordinary SQL and unencrypted database files. Do not replace an encrypted/custom engine with this route.

Initialize once at application startup before any SqliteConnection or database worker. Core alone does not select a native provider. Do not combine automatic bundle initialization with a different explicit provider.

Do not install Microsoft.Data.Sqlite alongside Core here: the wrapper selects its own e_sqlite3 bundle. Remove retired bundle references, including transitive ones, rather than mixing 2.x initialization assemblies with 3.x providers.

Direct Sqlite11 has net10.0 assets; EF11 independently needs net11.0. This edition advertises only its executed net11.0 current route; net10.0 is the previous-release comparison, not a new .NET10 foundation.

Encryption alternatives, paid native builds and platform-specific provider routes require their own exact graph, native features and existing-file/key compatibility proof. None is selected as a default product choice.
prerequisites: A writable temporary directory; samples create a unique disposable file, disable pooling, dispose connections and delete it in finally. No account, server, purchase or resource provisioning is needed.

Copy all six canonical files for one sample to its own directory, restore from nuget.org, then run from that directory so global.json applies. Lock files and verification records in the repository pin the observed graph. Initial dependency setup may need network access; served guidance is complete offline.
Samples have independent build/package boundaries, exact SDK/package pins and author-maintained lock files. Renovate permissions remain unchanged.
stabilityLimitations: Stable provider-initialization API; no experimental API or opt-in. Current managed package and SDK evidence is .NET11 RC2, not actual GA. Existing PIN-965 GA reconciliation and catalogue Human/release gates remain in place.
